newsitem.title: USA: CMI sees moderately lower yr oper earnings.
newsitem.headline: CMI sees moderately lower yr oper earnings.

text.p: CMI Corp said on Thursday it expected to report moderately lower operating earnings for the year ended December 31, 1996, on sales of about $138 million versus $130.6 million last year.
Operating earnings would be moderately lower than the $11.7 million earned in the prior year, CMI said.
The First Call mean earnings estimate for the fourth quarter was $0.05 per share and $0.34 per share for the year.
"A modest operating loss in the fourth quarter, including costs associated with its Load King division, decreased operating earnings for 1996 compared to the prior year," the company said.

For the quarter ended December 31, 1995, CMI had an operating loss of $204,000 and a net loss of $553,000 or $0.03 per share. For 1995, net earnings per share of $0.82 included a tax benefit of $0.55 per share. On a fully taxed basis, earnings would have been $0.27 per share for the year.
"This year's net income should be closed to the fully taxed equivalent of last year's," Jim Holland, chief financial officer, said.

The company, which designs and makes automated equipment for construction and maintenance of highways and streets, said sales of used equipment constributed to cash flow and sales in the fourth quarter 1996, but low margins in this area did not help the bottom line.
CMI also said 1996 revenues were hurt by uncertainty in Washington DC over prospects for government highway funding.
The Load King unit had costs of over $500,000 before taxes associated with a temporary workforce reduction, the company said. This equated to $0.02 per share in the quarter, it said.
Gross margins were unchanged in 1996, it said.
